terbaru.pelajaran: This paper presents a method for forecasting limit order book durations using a self-exciting flexible residual point process.

terbaru.pelajaran: This work deals with the estimation of parameters of Mittag-Leffler (ML($α, σ$)) distribution.

terbaru.judul: Temporal Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (T-KAN) for High-Frequency Limit Order Book Forecasting: Efficiency, Interpretability, and Alpha Decay
terbaru.pelajaran: In this paper, using data from the FI-2010 dataset, we introduce Temporal Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (T-KAN) to replace the fixed, linear weights of standard LSTMs with learnable B-spline activation functions.

terbaru.judul: Auctioning Time to Mitigate Latency Races: Theory and Evidence from Blockchains
terbaru.pelajaran: We show that auctioning artificial time priority can redirect resources away from wasteful speed races toward auction payments.

terbaru.judul: Predicting Price Movements in High-Frequency Financial Data with Spiking Neural Networks
terbaru.pelajaran: This work investigates the application of SNNs to high-frequency price-spike forecasting, enhancing performance via robust hyperparameter tuning with Bayesian Optimization (BO).

terbaru.judul: Emergence of Randomness in Temporally Aggregated Financial Tick Sequences
terbaru.pelajaran: We present a novel methodology to investigate ultra-high frequency financial data and to evaluate the extent to which tick by tick returns resemble random sequences.

terbaru.judul: When AI Trading Agents Compete: Adverse Selection of Meta-Orders by Reinforcement Learning-Based Market Making
terbaru.pelajaran: We investigate the mechanisms by which medium-frequency trading agents are adversely selected by opportunistic high-frequency traders.

To study these more general scenarios, we introduce the mathematical framework of latency-constrained games, which models time-evolving input and output processes for spatially separated parties subject to finite communication speeds.
